rows.source: HSE workplace oxygen fire and explosion controls
rows.verified: HSE guidance covers fire and explosion hazards for workplaces using oxygen gas cylinders.

rows.source: HSE workplace oxygen fire and explosion controls
rows.verified: Employers should include oxygen hazards and precautions in their workplace risk assessment.

rows.source: HSE workplace oxygen fire and explosion controls
rows.verified: Oxygen enrichment increases the ease and intensity with which materials can burn.

rows.source: HSE workplace oxygen fire and explosion controls
rows.verified: Oxygen-service equipment requires appropriate maintenance to prevent leaks, contamination and ignition.

rows.source: HSE workplace oxygen fire and explosion controls
rows.verified: Confined-space work involving oxygen needs controls against enrichment, fire and atmosphere hazards.

rows.source: HSE workplace oxygen fire and explosion controls
rows.verified: HSE lists oxygen use in the workplace as a distinct gas-safety and fire/explosion topic.

rows.source: HSE workplace oxygen fire and explosion controls
rows.verified: HSE fire-and-explosion resources include specific guidance on hazards arising from oxygen use.

rows.source: HSE workplace oxygen fire and explosion controls
rows.verified: Oxygen equipment must be used with precautions appropriate to oxygen-compatible service.

rows.source: HSE workplace oxygen fire and explosion controls
rows.verified: Oxygen risk depends on concentration, leakage, ventilation, equipment cleanliness, materials, pressure, ignition sources and confined-space conditions.

rows.source: HSE workplace oxygen fire and explosion controls
rows.verified: Oxygen evidence is equipment-, concentration-, material-, task- and environment-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire probability.

rows.source: HSE drum, gas-cylinder and dangerous-goods handling
rows.verified: A compressed or liquefied toxic-gas cylinder can present a significant personnel hazard despite its relatively small inventory.

rows.source: HSE drum, gas-cylinder and dangerous-goods handling
rows.verified: Pressurised cylinders should be secured and stored with their valves uppermost.

rows.source: HSE drum, gas-cylinder and dangerous-goods handling
rows.verified: Cylinder storage needs leak detection considerations, spill control, separation and emergency procedures.

rows.source: HSE drum, gas-cylinder and dangerous-goods handling
rows.verified: Compressed or liquefied gas cylinders require purpose-suitable transport such as cylinder trolleys or designed lift-truck attachments.

rows.source: HSE drum, gas-cylinder and dangerous-goods handling
rows.verified: Dangerous-goods drivers require general-awareness, function-specific and safety training under ADR requirements.

rows.source: HSE drum, gas-cylinder and dangerous-goods handling
rows.verified: Cylinder valves must be protected from damage when cylinders are carried horizontally.

rows.source: HSE drum, gas-cylinder and dangerous-goods handling
rows.verified: HSE lists design and inspection standards for transportable compressed-gas cylinders and cylinder bundles.

rows.source: HSE drum, gas-cylinder and dangerous-goods handling
rows.verified: When carrying a gas cylinder in a vehicle, the main cylinder valve should be closed to prevent leakage.

rows.source: HSE drum, gas-cylinder and dangerous-goods handling
rows.verified: Cylinder risk depends on gas properties, pressure, valve protection, restraint, storage layout, ventilation, transport method and emergency arrangements.

rows.source: HSE drum, gas-cylinder and dangerous-goods handling
rows.verified: Cylinder evidence is gas-, package-, pressure-, handling-, vehicle- and site-specific and is not an exact parcel-level release probability.
